h: Making the most of your splash
p: A couple of hours is usually the sweet spot at a flume park like this. It's long enough to work round every slide, go back to your favourites and still have energy left for the drive home, without anyone hitting that shivery, fed-up stage. If you've got a mix of ages, agree a plan before you go in: little ones in the splash zone with one adult, big kids and the brave grown-up on the flumes, then swap over halfway so nobody misses out.

Packing makes a big difference. Bring a towel each plus a spare, a bag for wet cossies, hair bobbles for long hair and a warm top for afterwards, because coming out of a heated pool into a breezy Dorset car park is a shock to the system. Babies and toddlers will need proper swim nappies, as you'd expect at any pool. Goggles are handy for the kids who hate water in their eyes, and a bottle of water and a snack for afterwards will head off the post-swim hunger meltdown.

Splashing about is hungry, thirsty work, so build in a proper refuel. Poole Quay is a good shout for an early tea with a view of the boats, and from the quay you can catch the ferry over to Brownsea Island on another day for red squirrels and woodland walks. Poole Park, with its big lake and open lawns, is another easy, free spot to let the kids run around once they've dried off.
